subject: Emotions
title: Food Taboos
description: A quick win: understand Food Taboos.

hook.text: Americans recoil at eating dogs. Chinese recoil at cheese. Every culture's 'gross' is another's delicacy.

buildup.text: Marvin Harris argued food taboos are ecological. Cows are sacred in India partly because they're more useful alive.

discovery.text: Insects are eaten by 2 billion people worldwide. Western disgust at bugs is a cultural anomaly, not a norm.

twist.text: Food companies now market cricket protein as 'flour' to bypass disgust. Rename it and people eat it.

climax.text: Food taboos prove that disgust is learnable and unlearnable. Culture programs what your body rejects.

punchline.text: Nothing is universally disgusting. Culture decides.

quiz.question: How many people eat insects worldwide?
